clue.text: See an object of hatred?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are looking at the thing they detest most.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is intense dislike or disgust, a strong synonym for hatred.

clue.text: Dial without hurrying?

parts.note: the four letters of this word are what you get by putting the word for 'set down' (... to front

explanation.surface: Turning a telephone dial in a slow, unhurried way.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the clue word is the result, and the answer is the instruction that produces it. LAID read backwards gives DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone relaxed and unhurried is easy-going, with no urgency about them.

clue.text: David's son joins sailor girl with order

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A biblical son links up with a seafarer and a young woman, and gets decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament, the rebel prince Absalom is a son of King David.

clue.text: French gentlemen in dance acting badly

indicators.note: in places the Frenchmen inside the word for the dance

parts.note: a hay is an old country dance
MM is the abbreviation for messieurs, French for gentlemen

explanation.surface: Some Frenchmen at a dance put on a terrible theatrical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The hay (or hey) is an old English country dance with weaving figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham actor overacts, so hammy describes exaggerated, poor stage performance.

clue.text: Given hug by loner, one about to be friendly?

indicators.note: about signals that the preceding letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A loner receives an embrace and is about to warm to people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal: HUG, BY, LONER and I (one) are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being neighbourly means acting kindly and helpfully towards those living nearby, a form of friendliness.

clue.text: Demeaned, one day, around HQ

indicators.note: around tells us the two short pieces go either side of the headquarters word

parts.note: one can be the article a
a base is a headquarters

explanation.surface: Someone humiliated around headquarters one day.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abased is to be lowered in dignity or humbled, which is to be demeaned.

clue.text: Have Indian dish with second helping in Maryland port

parts.note: a balti is a curry cooked and served in a metal pan, popular in British curry houses
asking for more means asking for a second helping

explanation.surface: An invitation to enjoy a curry and go back for seconds in an American harbour city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have' is just a link here, setting up the dinner-table picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is the largest city in the state of Maryland and a major seaport on Chesapeake Bay.

clue.text: Broadcast brief of warm weather?

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so we want a word that is pronounced like the one meaning brief

parts.note: a brief is a summary of facts or instructions

explanation.surface: A short weather forecast on air promising sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Summery describes the warm, sunny conditions typical of the hottest season.

clue.text: Stop believer restricting saint

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the believer word holds the saint inside

parts.note: a deist believes in God on grounds of reason

explanation.surface: An order to halt a person of faith who is holding back a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or leave off doing something.

clue.text: Complaint from one in gaudy mansion

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: gaudy suggests something showy and garish, so the letters are flashily rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble coming from someone living in a garish, showy house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaudy' is the anagram signal: I (one) and MANSION are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an ailment or disorder, and inability to sleep is one such condition.

clue.text: Clusters of cold swellings

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
lumps are swellings

explanation.surface: A medical description of groups of chilly bumps on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumps are compact groups of things gathered closely together, such as trees or plants.

clue.text: Corned beef — purchase about two pounds

indicators.note: about places the purchase word around the two pounds

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two pounds give two of them

explanation.surface: Buying a couple of pounds of tinned meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Bully beef is a British name for tinned corned beef, a military ration.
explanation.definitionFit: Bully, from the French bouilli, is canned corned beef, long a soldiers' staple.

clue.text: A certain throaty quality evident as old Nazi hosts American family

indicators.note: hosts means takes in as a guest, so the Nazi's name contains the other pieces

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy in the Nazi party
US is short for American, as in United States
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A gravelly voice heard when a wartime Nazi entertains an American household.
explanation.definitionFit: Huskiness is hoarseness or roughness of voice, a rasping sound from the throat.

clue.text: Look fair in brilliant illumination

parts.note: to search is to look for something
fair can mean light in colour, as of hair or skin

explanation.surface: Looking pretty in a dazzling glow.
explanation.definitionFit: A searchlight is a powerful lamp whose beam gives intense lighting over a distance.

clue.text: Committee member's speech of honour

parts.note: mem is a short form of member
oratory is formal public speaking

explanation.surface: A committee member delivers a formal speech of tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: Something commemoratory serves to honour and preserve the memory of a person or event.

clue.text: Language translated parents — Old English?

indicators.note: translated suggests turning into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether mum and dad's words have been rendered into an ancient tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' is the anagram signal: PARENTS and OE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international tongue created by L. L. Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: Tense and upset when Diana goes

indicators.note: goes means departs, so the short name is removed from the longer word

parts.note: distressed means upset
Di is a short form of the name Diana

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious and troubled when Diana leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stressed means being under strain, nervous and on edge.

clue.text: Softening charge for bond captivates hearts

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: captivates means holds captive, so the bond word encloses the hearts abbreviation

parts.note: to cement is to bond things together
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A legal charge relating to a financial bond wins people over.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapprochement is a re-establishment of friendly relations, a thawing or easing of hostility.

clue.text: Sea creature produces fear or qualms to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An animal of the ocean gives people some fear or doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: A rorqual is a baleen whale with throat grooves, such as the blue whale or fin whale.

clue.text: Competitive type in hospital department starting wild outburst

indicators.note: starting means the hospital department comes first, before the outburst

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
a rant is a wild, angry tirade

explanation.surface: A contestant in a hospital ward begins a furious tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who enters a contest, a competitor.

clue.text: Showing results of rash development, son gets mad

parts.note: potty is informal British for crazy

explanation.surface: A boy goes crazy after a hasty decision turns out badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotty skin is covered in pimples or blemishes, as a rash produces.

clue.text: Jamaican town produces drink fit for a king

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
royal means befitting a monarch

explanation.surface: A Caribbean place makes a beverage worthy of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Royal, at the end of the Palisadoes near Kingston, was once a notorious pirate haven.

clue.text: Tardy taking in hospital machine

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so the lateness word holds the hospital letter

parts.note: late means tardy
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A piece of hospital equipment arrives late.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine tool that rotates a workpiece so it can be shaped.

clue.text: To make a sudden thrust some call ungentlemanly

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some might call it rude to jab forward suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: To lunge is to move forward suddenly and forcefully, as with a sword in fencing.

clue.text: Endlessly loyal worker, but not one at school

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter of the loyalty word is dropped

parts.note: true means loyal or faithful
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A faithful employee who is nevertheless absent from class.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is a pupil who stays away from lessons without permission.

clue.text: A gun going off would, in short, get answer from some Africans

indicators.note: going off suggests the gun exploding, so its letters with A are blown into a new order

parts.note: would in its shortened form is 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A firearm discharging would, briefly, provoke a reaction from a group of Africans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' is the anagram signal: A and GUN give UGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugandans are people from Uganda, an East African nation, so they are some of the continent's people.

clue.text: Cowardly shouts of pain?

parts.note: to yell is to shout
ow is the cry one gives in pain

explanation.surface: Someone shrieking in agony is called spineless.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for lacking courage, as in 'yellow-bellied'.

clue.text: Watching cricket match with editor is warranted

parts.note: someone watching a Test, an international cricket match, is at Test

explanation.surface: Someone spectating at a cricket game with a newspaper editor is vouched for.
explanation.definitionFit: Attested means certified or vouched for, so it is guaranteed as true.
